title: Handle delayed webhook events and hourly usage late arrivals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We are seeing a class of invoice inaccuracies and quota misattribution caused by Stripe/ingestion webhooks that arrive after the hourly usage aggregation window has closed. When webhook arrival is delayed by network retries, regional failover, or downstream spikes, late events are currently either dropped by the hourly aggregator or stitched into the wrong billing window, causing: (1) proration skew on mid-cycle plan changes, (2) duplicate rate-limit credits on subsequent invoices, and (3) incorrect per-hour usage rollups that break chargeback and SLA reporting.

Observed failure modes:
- Webhook delivery >30 minutes after event timestamp due to transient backend queue saturation. Aggregator uses arrival time to bucket events, so late arrivals land in future hour.
- When backfill job runs, it merges late events but uses naive dedupe leading to duplicated invoice lines when a late arrive triggers both a rate-limit credit and a later reconciler export.
- Customers performing plan downgrades around the hour boundary see incorrect proration because usage meant for previous hour is billed against new plan rates.

Goal: Make the ingestion + aggregation pipeline resilient to delayed arrivals so invoice exports and NetSuite/Stripe reconciliation reflect true event-time usage. We must avoid duplication, preserve idempotency, and keep end-to-end latency reasonable.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Event-time bucketing: switch aggregator to primarily use event timestamp for initial bucket placement with a configurable late-arrival grace window. Default grace: 45 minutes.
2) Out-of-order handling: keep a transient 'late-buffer' per-hour that accepts late events up to the grace window; once the window expires, mark bucket immutable.
3) Deterministic dedupe: introduce a canonical usage event ID (stripe_event_id or generated stable hash) persisted with each usage row; backfill and reconciliation jobs must use the ID to dedupe.
4) Proration alignment: when a plan-change event exists within the same event-time bucket, ensure invoice proration computation is performed against event-time ordering (apply plan-change at its event timestamp) and run a mini-recompute for affected invoice lines if late events change the usage attribution.
5) Reconciler safety: modify billing export job to detect and suppress double-emit of credits if the target export is for the same canonical usage IDs already exported. Add an exported_signature field to NetSuite export state.
6) Monitoring & alerting: add metrics for late-arrival-rate, post-window-backfills, dedupe-suppressed-count, and invoice-diff-rate. Create a dashboard and an alert when late-arrival-rate > 0.5% for 3 hours.

Tradeoffs and constraints:
- Increasing grace window reduces misattribution but raises latency for final hourly aggregates and downstream dashboards. We choose 45m default with per-customer override for enterprise accounts.
- Persisting canonical IDs increases storage/indexing overhead and write paths; we will use a compact 16-byte hash and index on (customer_id, hour_bucket, event_id) only.
- Recomputing invoice lines on late arrival is expensive; limit recomputes to customers with non-zero balance delta > $1 or customers flagged for SLA sensitivity.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Design doc and schema changes (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/billing/late-arrival-2026) - complete.
- API contract updates: document that usage ingestion honors event_time and returns canonical_event_id.
- Aggregator change: event-time bucketing + late-buffer (feature flag: event_time_bucket_v2).
- Dedupe store: add canonical_event_id to usage table and expose dedupe APIs for backfill.
- Reconciler guard: add exported_signature and skip rules.
- End-to-end integration tests + chaos tests (simulate delayed webhooks and regional failover).
- Rollout: rollout behind feature flag, enable for 10% of tenants, monitor, then ramp.

Acceptance criteria:
- Less than 0.05% of usage records are re-assigned between buckets after finalization for rollout tenants.
- No duplicate credit lines emitted in NetSuite exports for rollout tenants.
- Proration mismatches related to hourly boundary downgrades reduced by 95% in sampled accounts.
- Metric pipeline reports late-arrival-rate and dedupe-suppressed-count in console.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Grace window too short => still misattribution. Mitigation: expose per-customer override and monitor.
- Risk: High cardinality index leads to perf regression. Mitigation: compact IDs, partial indexing, run load test (ENG-118900).
- Risk: Recompute churn generates invoice noise. Mitigation: threshold recompute to material deltas and notify customers via billing notes.

Rollout steps:
1) Merge aggregator changes behind feature flag + unit tests.
2) Deploy to staging and run synthetic delayed-webhook sim (test harness: GH PR #4321).
3) Enable for internal accounts + 1% production tenants for 24 hours; monitor metrics.
4) Ramp to 10% then 50% while watching invoice-diff-rate and dedupe-suppressed-count.
5) Full enable and deprecate legacy path after 4 weeks of stable metrics.

Related artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/billing/late-arrival-2026
- PR with aggregator changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4321
- Reconciler guard PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4399
- Integration test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/tree/main/integration/late-arrival-tests

Notes: This ticket focuses on the ingestion and reconciliation side. A separate follow-up (ENG-109200) will address UI/Support tooling to surface which invoices were affected and provide one-click invoice adjustment flow for CS teams.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Aisha Patel: Initial bug triage and data export attached to design doc. Observed ~0.8% of hourly aggregates had >1% re-assignment after late arrivals during last 30 days.
2026-02-20 - Marco Nguyen: POC for event-time bucketing completed. POC demonstrates 60% reduction in misattribution with 30m grace window. Pending schema review.
2026-02-27 - Schema review (Katherine Liu): Requested compacting event ID to 128-bit hash and adding partial index. Noted potential migration cost for existing usage rows.
2026-03-03 - Marco Nguyen: Began implementation of late-buffer. Feature flag event_time_bucket_v2 added. Unit tests for buffer closing logic in progress.
2026-03-06 - QA (Jon Ramos): Found race when backfill and live ingestion hit same bucket; adding optimistic locking and idempotency check to writer.

2026-03-10 - Marco Nguyen: Opened reconciler guard PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4399). Integration tests still flaky under high concurrency; increasing dedupe window and adding stronger test harness.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Marking for 1% canary on 2026-03-12 pending signoff from infra and QA.
